AtlasOfOne README explicitly describes its Worldwalker map and Worldwalker-era application baseline. This is an acknowledged product relationship, not proof of a package dependency.
The PWA Mapper README declares Star_System_Planner as its implementation repository. This is a documented implementation reference; no runtime package import was established.
edges.constraint: Implementation repository claim; no runtime dependency proven

edges.why: The PWA Mapper README names Starsilk_Character_Dossier as its strictly read-only canon reference. This is a source-authority dependency, not an editable data link.
edges.constraint: Read-only canon authority; never treat as permission to write

edges.why: The Monterey probe README states it was built to test the specific DexDictate SwiftWhisper/whisper.cpp path before porting the real app.

evidence.note: compatibility probe for DexDictate exact path

edges.why: A one-way, provenance-carrying export of stable WorldsVault identity and relationships could inform the draft map without inventing canonical coordinates.
edges.constraint: No coordinates invented. Read-only source. Approval required.

edges.why: Could show lineage entities as semantic overlays without treating Drakken biology as geography.
edges.constraint: Do not promote draft positions or biologic classifications to canon.

edges.why: Could hand a verified bounded edit plan or media export into a local production pipeline; no existing adapter was verified.
Could exchange a narrow, versioned shot contract between coordination and a tested rendering kernel.
edges.constraint: The kernel is not a generalized autonomous studio.

edges.why: A tested interchange could map rig keyframes into a still-sequence or motion-preset delivery pipeline.
edges.constraint: No shared interchange format has been verified.

edges.why: An approved read-only metadata export could supply project-state landmarks without importing private project details.
edges.constraint: Restrict to public metadata; do not equate commits with approval.

edges.why: GLB export might support user-approved world props if scale, materials, licenses and performance are verified.
edges.constraint: No actual asset compatibility test was run.

edges.why: AetherVFX runtime lifecycle patterns might be adapted to the outdoor Three.js world, subject to API and performance checks.
Hardware-accurate sprite-sheet outputs could become a tested demo input for the 2D browser toolkit.
Could reuse explicit local export and validation patterns in catalog tooling; similar libraries do not establish compatible code.
Could evaluate a shared approved character-motion asset pipeline, but the Dex Rig README explicitly says it does not replace or modify Dexter Desk Familiar.
edges.constraint: Approved likeness and animation fidelity must be verified; no shared asset proven.

edges.why: A rights-cleared sprite-format conversion could support familiar sprite studies, if actual assets are supplied and tested.
edges.constraint: No same-file or shared-asset hash established.

edges.why: The same user-owned image sequences could be processed by both media workbenches after explicit export/import testing.
edges.constraint: No existing shared storage or identical assets confirmed.

edges.why: Both documents describe simulated planetary worlds; a shared seed/assumptions comparison would be an experiment, not proven engine compatibility.
Both describe Drakken knowledge; a canon-linked dossier-to-lineage explainer could be built with strict authority and taxonomy checks.
edges.constraint: Do not infer written canon or morphology from visual similarity.
